candidate.derivedAnswer: E: Each segment is less than 1/2.
candidate.answerReason: Four positive lengths form a nondegenerate simple quadrilateral exactly when the longest is shorter than the sum of the other three. With total length 1, this is equivalent to every length being less than 1/2.

methods.label: Prove necessity and construct a shared diagonal
methods.explanation:
A side must be shorter than the broken path formed by the other three sides. We will also show that this restriction is enough to construct a quadrilateral.

Label the four positive lengths \(a\ge b\ge c\ge d>0\), with
\[
a+b+c+d=1.
\]
If they form a nondegenerate quadrilateral, the longest side satisfies
\[
a<b+c+d=1-a,
\]
so \(a<\tfrac12\). Thus every side is less than \(\tfrac12\). Equality would force the three-side path to lie along the longest side, giving a degenerate figure.

Conversely, suppose every length is less than \(\tfrac12\). We seek a diagonal of length \(t\) that can be shared by triangles with side lengths \(a,b,t\) and \(c,d,t\). The strict triangle inequalities require
\[
a-b<t<a+b,
\qquad c-d<t<c+d.
\]
Because \(a<\tfrac12\), we have \(a<b+c+d\), hence \(a-b<c+d\). Also \(c-d<c+d\), since \(d>0\), and \(c+d\le a+b\). Therefore the open interval
\[
\max(a-b,c-d)<t<c+d
\]
is nonempty, and every \(t\) in it allows both nondegenerate triangles.

Join the triangles on opposite sides of their common diagonal. Their boundary has the four prescribed side lengths and cannot cross itself. We can choose \(t\) so neither joined endpoint is a straight vertex: a straight vertex would fix the other diagonal as the sum of two given sides, fixing the remaining triangle by its three side lengths and hence fixing \(t\). Each endpoint therefore excludes at most one value, and the open interval contains other choices. Such a choice gives a nondegenerate simple quadrilateral.

Both directions are proved, so the necessary and sufficient condition is that each segment be \(\boxed{\text{less than }\tfrac12}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
